title: OpenClaw MCP -- T1567 operator custom headers forwarded across a cross-origin redirect
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-53840 (GHSA-rjxq-qqhf-8hwh,
CVSS 7.1 HIGH), a self-reported advisory for OpenClaw.

Prior to 2026.5.12, an MCP server configured with
`transportType: "streamable-http"` and operator-set custom headers
under `mcp.servers.*.headers` (e.g. an API key or tenant-routing
credential the operator needs the legitimate server to see) had those
headers forwarded automatically whenever the application followed an
HTTP redirect -- including a cross-origin one. A malicious, compromised,
or simply misbehaving MCP endpoint can respond to a request with a 3xx
redirect to an attacker-controlled origin; the client library follows
it and re-sends the SAME custom headers to the new destination,
exfiltrating the operator's configured secret to a domain it was never
meant to reach. The advisory notes this does not expose other,
unrelated OpenClaw credentials -- only the specific custom headers
configured for that MCP server.

Detection logic flags the PRECONDITION this advisory's chain depends
on, since neither the specific custom header name nor the legitimate
MCP server's host is fixed by the vulnerable code (both are
per-deployment operator configuration, and the advisory names neither
as a literal example) -- an MCP `streamable-http` connection whose
response is a cross-origin redirect (a 3xx status with a `Location`
pointing at a different host than the one the client connected to) is
the one host-observable, deployment-independent signal the vulnerable
client library acts on before forwarding headers. This is a narrower,
more honest claim than "headers were exfiltrated" -- it flags "the
exact condition this bug turns dangerous" fired, not confirmed leakage.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (openclaw, via
GHSA and VulnCheck's corroborating write-up), fixed in 2026.5.12.
